about.title: San Marcos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Marcos sits along SR-78 in San Diego County, and that highway appears more often than any other road in the city's collision records. W San Marcos Boulevard, S Rancho Santa Fe Road and N Twin Oaks Valley Road follow behind it. In 2025, the most recent finalized reporting year, San Marcos logged 270 injury collisions. Those crashes left 386 people hurt and three people dead. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. produce the largest cluster of reports, which tracks with the end-of-week commute. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow matter. Insurers move quickly, sometimes calling before you have finished treatment, and California's pure comparative fault rule means anything you say about blame can shave a percentage off what you recover. We handle San Marcos car accident cases on contingency. You pay nothing for a free case review, and we collect a fee only if there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why San Marcos Drivers Choose Us

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county or Caltrans vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Our team will sort out which clock applies to your San Marcos crash.

items.title: Comparative Fault Is Handled Carefully
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault system, your recovery is reduced by whatever share of blame is assigned to you, even if that share is small. We work to keep the record accurate and to push back on the other insurer's version of events.

items.title: No Damage Cap, No Upfront Fee
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. We take these matters on contingency, so you owe a fee only if there is a recovery.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-78 in San Marcos. Does that change anything about my claim?
items.answer: It can. SR-78 is a state highway, so if road design, signage or a Caltrans vehicle played any role, part of your claim might be against a government entity, and that triggers a much shorter notice window, sometimes six months. Even in a straightforward driver-versus-driver collision, freeway crashes often involve multiple vehicles and overlapping insurance policies. We can identify every responsible party early so nothing lapses.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and most attorneys will advise against it. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that produce answers usable to assign you a share of fault under comparative negligence. Politely decline, and let our team handle that communication.

items.question: What should I keep or gather after a San Marcos car accident?
items.answer: Save photos of the vehicles, the roadway and your injuries, along with the police report number and the names of any witnesses. Keep every medical bill, prescription receipt and pay stub showing missed work. If a nearby business on San Marcos Boulevard or Rancho Santa Fe Road may have camera footage, note it quickly, because many systems overwrite within days.
